entities.summary: Filippo Gagliardi was an Italian painter of the Baroque period, active mainly in Rome, who specialized in painting architecture. He collaborated with Filippo Lauri, Andrea Sacchi and Giovanni Benedetto Castiglione. He also helped in the renovation of San Martino ai Monti (1647–1654). He contributed illustrated architectural perspectives to Ferrari's Hesperides (1646). He was a member of the Accademia di San Luca from at least 1638 and became principe in 1656–1658. He was also a member of the Congregazione dei Virtuosi del Pantheon.
